entries.value: Keller ‘PIUS’ Auslese Rheinhessen 2022 is a sweet Auslese made from late harvest and botrytis-touched grapes, the varieties changing with the vintage, from a family estate at Flörsheim-Dalsheim. It tastes of honeyed apricot, pineapple and spice, rich and pure, held up by stony acidity. Its fruit matches the charred pineapple and its acidity keeps the puff pastry and the anglaise light, so it is the half bottle for the Pineapple Tarte Tatin. We pour 2 to 3 oz at 45 to 50°F in a small dessert glass, then recork it and keep it cold. Weingut Keller made its name with dry Riesling, and this is its sweet side.
entries.reason: Five-star review of the description: it opened on the estate, not the wine, and named the New Orleans Bread Pudding and the Lemon Tart, neither of whose pairings names this wine; it now opens on the wine as the list prints it and names only the tarte Tatin

entries.value: Opus One Napa Valley 2015 is one grand vin from Oakville, blended from Cabernet Sauvignon and the other Bordeaux grapes, with Cabernet in the lead. It shows blackcurrant, black cherry, cocoa, violet and graphite, with polished tannin, a long finish and the first savoury notes of age. Its tannin wants protein, so it suits beef and a celebration for two. We pour it at 60 to 64°F in a large Bordeaux glass, decanted briefly or swirled well: two or three glasses. Opus One began as a partnership of Napa and Château Mouton Rothschild, and its first vintage was 1979, the first such venture between Bordeaux and California.

entries.value: Château d’Yquem Sauternes 2015 is led by Sémillon, with Sauvignon Blanc, from grapes noble rot has shrivelled, taken berry by berry as the pickers pass through the vines many times; in poor years no Yquem is made. The 2015 tastes of apricot, candied orange, saffron, honey and vanilla, luscious, with fresh acidity and a very long finish. Its richness meets the mascarpone mousse and raspberry coulis, so it is the celebration bottle for the Framboise French Toast. We pour 2 to 3 oz at 50 to 54°F in a white wine glass and recork it. The 1855 classification gave Yquem a rank of its own, Premier Cru Supérieur.

entries.value: Château d’Yquem Sauternes 2016 is Sémillon with Sauvignon Blanc, left on the vine until noble rot shrivels it, the pickers returning again and again to take it berry by berry. The 2016 is bright: candied lemon, apricot, pineapple, honey and spice. A dessert wine must be sweeter than the dessert; Yquem stays above the lemon jelly and yuzu mousse while its acidity matches the citrus, so it is the celebration bottle for the Lemon Tart. We pour 2 to 3 oz at 50 to 54°F in a white wine glass and recork it. The Lur-Saluces family married into the estate in 1785 and held it for two centuries.
